programmes.d: On Valentines Day, Kelly hauls in a load of Valentines, while Steve plans to give Marcy a trip to Hawaii. When Marcy finds out from Peggy, she plans to give Steve his Valentine present by jumping out of a life-size cake.
The Bundy's stay at the shoe store after their house is tented for termites. A grounded Kelly plots to escape and go to a rock concert.
Marcy regrets denting Steve's new car when he claims that she's made him impotent.

While secretly going through Steve and Marcy's mail, Al and Peggy fill out an application to a TV game show called "How Do I Love Thee" where the objective is a Bundy natural: surviving physical torture from one's spouse.
John takes Reggies advice to be more sensitive with women. It helps at the office with Margaret, but backfires with a woman he is dating.
John is surprised when a patient is disappointed at the news that he's not terminally ill. Jake scams Bob in a Scrabble game.
Reggie goes out to dinner with her abusive friend Sara and Sara's husband, Richard. She finds that she and Richard are attracted to each other.
John tries to keep a casual love affair alive, while Bob tries to turn a found Super Bowl ring into his ticket to fame and fortune.
John believes that Christmas is a phony time of the year. Instead of embracing the Christmas spirit, he uses getting robbed as vindication for his position.
Reggie meets Johns's friend Dan, who is recently divorced from an extraordinary, accomplished woman.
Becker and the crew decide to barter services office visits for food and services.
Becker obsesses over whether or not younger women still find him attractive. Linda takes advantage of a hard-working temp.
Becker gets in hot water with parents when his nutrition lecture at an elementary school turns into a sex talk.
John gets a portable talking computer for his speech-impaired patient, with unintended consequences.
An infomercial sparks Doug¹s (Kevin James) interest and he is quick to purchase the featured product.
Doug (Kevin James) and Carrie (Leah Remini) are down on their luck; Carrie is still out of a job, money is tight and the refrigerator is broken.

Doug (Kevin James) and Carrie (Leah Remini) decide its only fair that Deacon (Victor Williams) and Kelly (Merrin Dungey) occasionally watch Arthur (Jerry Stiller) in exchange for babysitting their kids.

Carrie (Leah Remini) befriends Trish (Janeane Garofalo) an ex-girlfriend of Doug’s (Kevin James) in order to get a discount at Saks, but soon realizes why he dumped her-she is extremely needy and says the word 'literally' in every sentence.
While recovering in the hospital from an emergency appendectomy, Doug (Kevin James) is caught moaning the names of several women in his sleep.
Doug (Kevin James) is unhappy with his new delivery route, specifically one nearly naked man who reveals too much.
Doug (Kevin James) shuns Deacon (Victor Williams) and bumps Danny (Gary Valentine) up to best-friend status after finding out Deacon has been playing racquetball with his grade school archenemy.
Carrie (Leah Remini) doesn’t want to stay with Doug’s (Kevin James) parents while visiting them in Florida.
When Adam discovers that the pastor he hired for their wedding was a phony and he and Andi aren't really married, he scrambles to find a way to fix it before she finds out.
When the kids won't do their chores, Adam and Andi decide to go on strike too.
When Adam thinks Kate's boyfriend, Tyler (Griffin Gluck), is a pothead, he decides to confront Tyler but doesn't get the support he expects from Andi.
When Adam needs to hire a new project manager, Andi accuses Adam of unconscious bias after he only interviews men for the job.
Adam and Andi try to get back in their neighbors' good graces after no one shows up to their potluck.
When Adam and Andi are caught off guard by unexpected expenses, they each decide to give up a luxury to pay them off.
When Adam takes his kids to work with him for the day, they accidentally give his biggest client lice. Also, Andi feels like a bad mom when she's the only one in the family not to get lice.
When Adam notices his Dad's increasingly forgetful behavior, he struggles with how to approach him to discuss it.
Joe and Helen meet the famous architect Y.M. Burg, who out of sympathy offers to design their new traditional dream home. Brian hires a new mechanic with a secret.

Brian gains over a hundred pounds and is forced to join Eat-A-Holics, where he realizes that his outrageous weight gain is because he feels rejected by his recently married brother, Joe, now that Joe has less time to spend with him.
Helen and Joe fight over the plans for their new home and Joe has a terrible dream that seems like reality.
Helen throws her first Christmas party and all of her guests have their wallets stolen.
Helen and Joe baby-sit their friend's little girl and dump their childhood neuroses on her.
Joe and Brian are reunited with their grandfather, Jack Hackett, who Helen and Casey discover is an imposter.

R.J., Roy Biggins' estranged gay son, returns to Nantucket to celebrate his father's birthday and confronts him about his lifestyle.
Fay decides to marry after a whirlwind romance with a man she met on a cruise ship.
Returning from an idyllic honeymoon in the sunny tropics, Joe and Helen learn their house has burned to the ground.
Joe is indignant about throwing his brother, Brian, out of his life until he receives a visit from the ghost of his father.
Joe and Brian are paid to fly the deceased old man Kingsbury back to Nantucket and accidentally bring back the wrong body so Joe has to pose as a corpse.

Lowell returns to Nantucket after seeing America and immediately needs to fly to Boston to repair one of Roy's planes. While in Boston, Lowell witnesses a gangland murder and is forced to enter the Federal Witness Protection Program.
Carrie and Doug have four tickets for a month to the Knicks games and try to find the perfect couple to join them.
Deacon and Dog fight over a childhood toy.
Deacon wants to give his kids a great Thanksgiving but can't do it all by himself. Doug loans him Carrie. Carrie turns out to be more than Deacon bargained for.
While Doug and Carrie are on vacation with friends, Arthur calls Doug to say there's a mold problem in the basement that will cost $ 7,000 to fix.

There has been a rash of burglaries in the area, and the Rhodes' house is robbed and Al's car stereo is ripped off. Steve and Marcy buy a guard dog that won't stop barking, and Al purchases a fire arm. Ultimately, the two methods of home defense clash.
Al and Steve buy a beat up Ford Mustang off of one of Kelly's boyfriends. Soon they form a tight friendship while fixing it up like new. The only problem is they are neglecting their wives.
Steve and Marcy plan to add a new room onto their house using their tax refund money. Al convinces Steve to make it into a billiards room while Peggy convinces Marcy to make it into an exercise room.
